text:
anya (oncall): seeing etcd commit latency spike ap-south-1 (~700ms) and apiserver 502s in multiple AZs. controller-manager restarted twice. GPU onboarding backlog growing, pods Pending. anyone picking this up? :grimacing:

gabe: SNAT ephemeral ports reported near exhaustion at 14:02. artifact pipeline pushed large uploads around same time. could be egress throttling affecting snapshot uploads and WAL flush.

tess: quick check of etcd pods:
```
# kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l app=etcd -o wide
etcd-aps1-0   1/1 Running   0  45m  10.10.2.5  ap-s1a
etcd-aps1-1   0/1 CrashLoop 6  34m  10.10.3.7  ap-s1b
```

cloud: opening support case; increasing SNAT table and enabling a short IOPS burst for etcd leader. case 992344.

anya (oncall): mitigation plan: (1) pause artifact uploads, (2) reduce controller concurrency, (3) add small relaxed-taint GPU nodepool to drain Pending, (4) monitor etcd leader.

tess: patching controller-manager args now:
```bash
kubectl -n kube-system patch deploy kube-controller-manager --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kube-controller-manager","args":["--concurrent-deployment-syncs=1","--concurrent-job-syncs=1"]}]}}}}'
```

infra-bot: alert: etcd_commit_latency > 500ms (ap-south-1) - created INC-5077.

gabe: cloud applied SNAT bump and 4x iops burst for 45m. they also recommended delaying large snapshot uploads until SNAT stabilizes.

tess: spun up spot-gpu-aps1-relaxed pool and cordoned noisy test nodes. GPU Pending down ~60% in 8m, apiserver 5xxs falling to baseline.

anya (oncall): good recovery. follow-ups: add runbook step to pause artifact streams when etcd_commit_latency > 300ms, consider permanent SNAT capacity increase for ap-south-1, and test follower read endpoints for heavy watchers. keeping incident open for 30m.
